facts.statement: The study used a retrospective design to look at patients who received repeat stereotactic radiosurgery between 2016 and 2025.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The researchers analyzed data from 96 patients who had a total of 132 recurrent brain metastases.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Patients receiving a second course of radiation had a 78.7% local control rate at 12 months, while those receiving a third course had a 67.0% rate.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The median time without local tumor progression after the second radiation course was 47.1 months.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Radiological signs of radiation-induced brain damage occurred in 40.9% of patients after the second treatment course.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Symptoms caused by radiation damage appeared in 14.6% of patients, but all of them got better after taking corticosteroids.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study found no deaths directly caused by the treatment.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors note that future forward-looking studies are required to better select patients and predict risks.
facts.subject: humans
